form.en: yuefu ballad with lines of mixed length

text_note.zh: 语文课本的文字和这里所用的古籍本有几处不同：“金尊”课本作“金樽”，“投筯”作“投箸”，“拔劒”作“拔剑”，“多岐路”作“多歧路”，这些只是写法不同。另外古籍本作“雪暗天”“坐溪上”，课本作“雪满山”“碧溪上”。这里用课本的文字。
text_note.en: The school textbook text differs from the old edition used here in a few places. Some are only different ways of writing the same word: the cup, the chopsticks, the sword and the forking roads. Two are real wording changes: the old edition has "snow darkens the sky" and "sit by the stream", while the textbook has "snow covers the mountains" and "by the green stream". We follow the textbook.

readings.zh: “斗”在这里读 dǒu，是量酒的单位。“斗十千”是说一斗酒值十千钱。
readings.en: Here this character is read dǒu, a unit for measuring wine. Dǒu shí qiān means one dǒu of wine costs ten thousand coins.

readings.zh: “塞”在这里读 sè，意思是堵住。
readings.en: Here this character is read sè, meaning to block up.

readings.zh: “太行”是山名，“行”读 háng，不读 xíng。
readings.en: Tàiháng is the name of a mountain range, so this character is read háng, not xíng.

glosses.zh: 金樽：金子做的酒杯，这里指精美的酒杯。
glosses.en: jīn zūn: a golden wine cup; here, a fine, costly cup.

glosses.zh: 斗十千：一斗酒值十千钱，就是一万钱。形容酒非常贵。
glosses.en: dǒu shí qiān: a dǒu of wine costs ten thousand coins. It means the wine is very expensive.

glosses.zh: 珍羞：珍贵的菜肴。“羞”同“馐”，是美味的食物。
glosses.en: zhēn xiū: rare, delicious dishes. Xiū here means fine food.

glosses.zh: 投箸：放下筷子。箸，就是筷子。
glosses.en: tóu zhù: to put down the chopsticks. Zhù means chopsticks.
sì gù: to look all around.

glosses.zh: 茫然：心里空空的，不知道该怎么办。
glosses.en: máng rán: at a loss, not knowing what to do.

glosses.zh: 冰塞川：冰把河道堵住了。川，河流。
glosses.en: bīng sè chuān: ice blocks the river. Chuān means river.

glosses.zh: 太行：太行山，在今天的山西、河北、河南交界一带。
glosses.en: Tàiháng: the Taihang Mountains, where today's Shanxi, Hebei and Henan meet.

glosses.zh: 闲来垂钓碧溪上：用了姜太公的故事。传说吕尚（姜太公）年老时在渭水边钓鱼，遇到了周文王，后来帮周朝打下天下。
glosses.en: xián lái chuí diào bì xī shàng: this recalls the story of Lü Shang, also called Jiang Taigong. Legend says that in old age he fished by the Wei River, met King Wen of Zhou, and later helped the Zhou win the land.

glosses.zh: 乘舟梦日边：用了伊尹的故事。传说伊尹被商汤请去做官前，梦见自己坐船经过太阳和月亮旁边。“日边”也暗指皇帝身边。
glosses.en: chéng zhōu mèng rì biān: this recalls the story of Yi Yin. Legend says that before King Tang of Shang called him to serve, he dreamed of sailing past the sun and moon. "Beside the sun" also hints at being beside the emperor.
qí lù: forking roads, roads that split apart.
ān zài: where is it? Ān means where.

glosses.zh: 长风破浪：乘着大风冲破巨浪。南朝宋的宗悫小时候说过：“愿乘长风破万里浪。”比喻实现远大的志向。
glosses.en: cháng fēng pò làng: riding a great wind to break through huge waves. As a boy, Zong Que of the Southern Dynasties said he wished to ride the long wind and break waves ten thousand miles long. It stands for reaching a great goal.

glosses.zh: 云帆：高高的船帆，像天上的云一样。
glosses.en: yún fān: a tall sail, high as the clouds.

glosses.zh: 济沧海：渡过大海。济，渡过。沧海，青色的大海。
glosses.en: jì cāng hǎi: to cross the wide blue sea. Jì means to cross.

translation.zh: 金杯里盛着清酒，一斗要卖十千钱，
translation.en: Clear wine fills golden cups, ten thousand coins a measure;

translation.zh: 玉盘里装着美味的菜，价值一万钱。
translation.en: Fine dishes fill jade plates, worth ten thousand coins.

translation.zh: 我却放下酒杯，丢下筷子，吃不下去，
translation.en: But I set down my cup, throw down my chopsticks, and cannot eat;

translation.zh: 拔出宝剑向四周看，心里一片茫然。
translation.en: I draw my sword and look all around, lost in my heart.

translation.zh: 想渡过黄河，冰块堵住了河道；
translation.en: I want to cross the Yellow River, but ice blocks the stream;

translation.zh: 想登上太行山，大雪盖满了山。
translation.en: I want to climb the Taihang Mountains, but snow covers the peaks.

translation.zh: 闲下来时，像姜太公一样在碧绿的溪边钓鱼，
translation.en: At leisure I fish by a green stream, like Jiang Taigong of old;

translation.zh: 忽然又像伊尹一样，梦见坐船经过太阳旁边。
translation.en: Then suddenly, like Yi Yin, I dream of sailing beside the sun.
So many forks in the way,

translation.zh: 总有一天我会乘着大风冲破巨浪，
translation.en: A day will come when I ride the long wind and break the waves,

translation.zh: 挂起高高的船帆，渡过茫茫大海。
translation.en: Hoist my cloud-high sail, and cross the wide blue sea.

background.zh: 《行路难》是乐府旧题，原来多写世路艰难和离别的伤感。李白一共写了三首，这是第一首。一般认为，这组诗写于唐玄宗天宝三年（744年）。李白曾被召到长安，做了翰林供奉，想在朝廷里大干一番，可是受到权贵排挤，最后被皇帝“赐金放还”，就是给一笔钱让他离开。临走时朋友们设宴送行，李白写下了这首诗。一说写于他第一次去长安失意而归的时候。
background.en: "Hard Is the Road" is an old yuefu title. Poems under it usually told of how hard life is, and of the pain of parting. Li Bai wrote three, and this is the first. They are usually dated to 744. Li Bai had been called to Chang'an to serve at court, and he hoped to do great things. But powerful men pushed him out, and in the end the emperor gave him money and sent him away. Friends held a farewell feast, and Li Bai wrote this poem. Another view says it was written after his first trip to Chang'an, which also ended in failure.

author_note.zh: 李白（701—762），字太白，号青莲居士，唐代最有名的诗人之一，被称为“诗仙”。他从小就有远大的理想，想像古代的贤人一样帮助君王治理天下。可他一生在官场都不顺利。他的诗想象大胆，感情奔放，即使写失意，也总带着一股不服输的豪气。
author_note.en: Li Bai (701–762) is one of the most famous Tang poets, called the Immortal of Poetry. From a young age he dreamed of helping a ruler govern the land, like the wise men of old. But his life at court never went well. His poems are bold and full of feeling, and even when he writes of failure, they carry a spirit that will not give up.

appreciation.zh: 开头是一桌豪华的宴席：金杯里的美酒，玉盘里的好菜。可李白一口也吃不下，拔出剑来四处张望，心里空荡荡的。为什么？接下来两句说出了原因：他想渡黄河，河被冰封住；想登太行，山被雪盖住。这是在比喻他想做事，路却被堵死了。但他不肯灰心，想到姜太公钓鱼、伊尹做梦，这些人后来都被君王重用，也许自己也还有机会。可是眼前的路那么多岔口，到底该往哪走？“行路难”连喊两遍，像一声声叹气。最后两句却突然振作起来：总有一天，我会乘风破浪，挂起高帆，渡过大海！全诗情绪一会儿低落，一会儿昂扬，起伏很大，最后落在希望上，读起来让人也跟着振奋起来。
appreciation.en: The poem opens on a grand feast: fine wine in golden cups, rich food on jade plates. But Li Bai cannot eat a bite. He draws his sword and stares around him, empty inside. Why? The next two lines tell us. He wants to cross the Yellow River, but it is frozen. He wants to climb the Taihang Mountains, but they are buried in snow. This is a picture of his life: he wants to act, but every road is blocked. Still he will not lose heart. He thinks of Jiang Taigong fishing and Yi Yin dreaming. Both were later trusted by kings, so maybe he still has a chance. Yet the road splits so many ways. Which one should he take? He cries "Hard is the road!" twice, like two deep sighs. Then the last two lines suddenly lift: one day I will ride the wind, break the waves, raise my sail and cross the sea! The feeling swings low and high, and ends on hope. Reading it, you feel lifted too.
